replacements.from: This is the cleanest positive of the program, and it is the interventional definition of commitment the campaign has been circling: the organism's future becomes progressively harder to move with a fixed dose, the loss of movability is aligned to a turn computable from the organism's own past, and no future information enters the turn rule.
replacements.to: The same fixed intervention has less influence later in development. In this reused cohort, that decline also aligns with a structural turn calculated from the untouched past; it does not establish that the score itself causes the loss of influence.

replacements.from: We froze four predeclared experiments to pin down what commitment means in a developing Flow Lenia creature: a fresh-cohort confirmation of the fine-shape result, a steerability profile across developmental passage, a basin-width measurement under initial-condition variation, and a history-disambiguation curve. The push stopped working on schedule, the sibling fan kept opening, the population of look-alikes emptied out, and the headline we came to confirm did not confirm.
replacements.to: Does a developing body resist intervention because its possible forms are narrowing? Four experiments separate those questions. The same push had less effect at later ages, but sibling shapes spread farther apart. A fresh-cohort test also failed to confirm the earlier fine-shape result.

replacements.from: Every experiment below wrote its plan.json before a single outcome run existed, in the campaign's write-once style with SHA-256 bindings between code, tests, and upstream artifacts, and each primary is a single frozen rule that secondaries cannot rescue. Nothing fresh remained on either allocation axis of the compact sweep, so the plans say so out loud: the steerability, basin, and disambiguation experiments reuse the f33-f48 solo block with the reuse disclosed in every plan, and the confirmation experiment generated genuinely fresh material by extending the original sweep with 512 new seeds under byte-identical search parameters.
replacements.to: Each experiment fixed its primary comparison before outcomes were run. The intervention-age, sibling-width, and history comparisons reused the same sixteen families. Only the fine-shape confirmation used a new cohort, generated from 512 additional sweep seeds with unchanged search parameters.

replacements.from: Read together, the two misses carry the program's real finding. Development in this substrate does not funnel siblings toward a shared template, it walks each one into a region of shape space increasingly its own, which is why look-alikes become scarce with age while the width of the sibling fan grows. Commitment, measured interventionally in the steerability profile, coexists with divergence measured observationally here: each organism becomes rigid about its own course precisely while the courses spread apart.
replacements.to: Sibling shapes spread farther apart as development proceeds, and fewer pairs remain within the fixed shape-matching radius. Meanwhile, the same intervention produces less downstream change. Declining sensitivity to a push therefore coexists with growing variation among siblings.

replacements.from: The word commitment suggested a narrowing, a possibility space closing around a target form, and the basin experiment was designed to watch the narrowing happen. What the four verdicts support instead is a two-part statement: after a turn that the organism's own past announces, an equal push moves the future less and less, and at the same time nothing about the population converges, since siblings spread and look-alikes vanish. The organism does not settle into a mold. It becomes a specific individual that holds its own course against the same perturbation that once redirected it.
replacements.to: The results support a specific distinction: later bodies are less sensitive to the tested intervention, but their forms do not converge. This does not imply resistance to every intervention, and the fresh fine-shape confirmation remains unresolved.

replacements.from: A creature that cannot be pushed off course, whose siblings do not converge, and whose look-alikes disappear is not narrowing toward a template. It is becoming harder to argue with about a future only it is heading into. That is what commitment turned out to mean when we measured it four ways at once.
replacements.to: A fixed push, sibling variation, matched histories, and a fresh confirmation measure different things. Keeping those comparisons separate is what reveals the result: reduced sensitivity to intervention does not require convergence on one form.

replacements.from: This changes the target. There may be no universal magic texture. The organism appears to have a private hidden coordinate system: the ability to be redirected is shared, while the meaningful direction must be learned from its own development.
replacements.to: The decoy produced a comparable response. The experiment establishes sensitivity to hidden composition, but does not show that the imported field has a unique developmental effect in these organisms.

replacements.from: The causal action world was already present in early material. Spatial organization did something subtler and more organism-like: it made nearby actions more legible, development faster and more reliable, and distant futures less explosive.
replacements.to: At passage 8, we rearranged the same material at three spatial scales and applied matched challenges. Disorganization delayed formation, reduced the consistency of nearby interventions, and increased separation among distant futures. The comparison asks what spatial arrangement contributes beyond the material itself.

replacements.from: That is directly relevant to causal emergence. It suggests that the interesting precursor may not be a scalar “more information” peak. It may be the onset of canalization: the moment distributed structure begins to make interventions have stable, coordinated meanings for the future of the whole.
replacements.to: The control separates spatial arrangement from total material. It does not identify a universal information score: it shows that preserving spatial relationships changes how these early fields respond to intervention.

replacements.from: Before a persistent body is visible, a developing Flow Lenia field already responds differently to nearby interventions. Later, the same push has less influence—yet sibling runs keep reaching different shapes.
replacements.to: A developing Lenia body becomes less sensitive to the same disturbance, even as runs with the same rule grow into different shapes. To understand that combination, we follow how its responses change before and after a coherent body appears.

replacements.from: We began by asking whether a disturbed run could recover the organization and trajectory of its undisturbed counterpart. That recovery was not clean or consistent. Following the different futures instead led to the experiments below: forecasts, branching interventions, feedback, and hidden-state rewrites.
replacements.to: A still image shows where the matter is. It cannot show how that matter will respond when its surroundings change. In Flow Lenia, we can copy an exact developing state, disturb one copy, and compare the two as they continue. Repeating this at different ages lets us ask how a body acquires a characteristic response, and whether becoming harder to change also makes its development more predictable.

Timing and spatial leverage harden while sibling shapes spread farther apart, so becoming harder to rewrite does not mean converging on one body.
replacements.to: Resistance to a disturbance and convergence on a common form might seem like two signs of the same developmental stability. Here they separate. That distinction leads us back to the early field: before a coherent body has formed, what already constrains its later responses? The experiments below follow those constraints through development, then test how far feedback and changes in hidden composition can redirect them.

replacements.from:
Passage numbers count forward from the seeded starting field. Passages 8, 12, and later checkpoints are scheduled observations, not life stages inferred from appearance.

01 · how we looked

One visible field can have different futures.

A visible Flow Lenia frame shows where the matter is, although it does not show all of the channel composition hidden beneath that sum, nor does it tell us which nearby futures remain reachable; we therefore compared forecasts, interventions, and later responses from the same exact checkpoints.
replacements.to:
01 · following the response

What the visible body leaves out

The visible field adds together the matter in Flow Lenia’s channels. Different channel mixtures can therefore produce the same picture. Because those channels interact differently, a matching image need not imply a matching future.

We count simulation passages from the seeded starting field and save states at scheduled checkpoints. Repeating the comparison at later passages follows the same rule and developing field through time.

replacements.from: One instrument, which we call whole-over-parts, compares how well the full state forecasts its next state with how well the strongest tested separable split forecasts it; when this difference rises, the whole is catching up with that split, although in the prospective precursor its absolute level remains negative and the best split still forecasts better at every measured phase. This is a forecasting comparison inspired by GARD and related compositional questions, not an identification with IIT Φ.
replacements.to: To ask whether spatial regions become more informative about one another as a body forms, we compare two forecasts. One uses the measured state jointly; the other divides it into parts and treats those groups independently. We choose the strongest tested split as the comparator. The difference, which we call whole-over-parts, measures how much predictive information the joint description gains or loses relative to that split.

replacements.from: Because one score could easily mistake a convenient coordinate for a cause, we also intervened directly: we branched exact futures from the same checkpoint, applied matched writes at different ages, ran feedback policies and then released them, and swapped hidden channel composition while holding the visible field exactly fixed. The account that follows depends on where these different views agree, and it keeps their disagreements visible when they do not.
replacements.to:
If the difference rises before coherent form appears, interactions among the measured regions may be changing in a way that the outline does not capture. That is what the prospective comparison found: the joint forecast closed part of its deficit, although the best split remained ahead. The score is inspired by GARD’s whole-versus-parts question; it is not a measurement of IIT Φ.

A changing forecast does not tell us what controls development. For that, we return to the saved states and intervene. By comparing each disturbed continuation with an untouched copy, we measure the consequences of the intervention directly. Hidden-channel rewrites make this especially revealing: the initial picture can remain exactly the same while the later body changes. These comparisons connect the information measurement to a physical question about how the field maintains and changes its organization.
